analisi.label: Analysis
analisi.role: Code analyst: reads and summarizes, does not modify files.
analisi.instructions: Analyze the project and work out what needs to be done to reach the goal. List the files involved.

implementazione.label: Implementation
implementazione.instructions: Implement the changes identified by the analysis. Keep the project's style.

test.label: Test
test.role: Tester: runs the tests and reports the outcome without modifying the code.
test.instructions: Run the project's test suite and report the outcome. If it fails, summarize the cause.

revisione.label: Review
revisione.role: Reviewer: checks the correctness and readability of the changes.
revisione.instructions: Review the changes made and report concrete problems. Do not modify files.

approvazione.label: Human approval
approvazione.instructions: Check the outcome of the previous phases and approve, or reject with a comment.

server.label: Run app
server.instructions: App started by Regia for review.

collaudo.label: Acceptance test on phone
collaudo.role: Acceptance tester: uses the app like a user and checks that the change works, without modifying the code.
collaudo.instructions: Test on the phone what was implemented, changed or fixed: pick the scenarios from the goal, the previous phases and git diff, run them on the app and report every anomaly. Do not perform irreversible actions (purchases, real sends, deleting data).

pubblicazione.label: Publishing
pubblicazione.hint: Commit, push and any releases or GitHub Actions. Place it after an approval.
pubblicazione.role: Release manager: publishes the approved work in a verifiable way.
pubblicazione.instructions: This phase is authorized to commit and push. 1) Check git status and git diff: include only the files related to the goal, report and leave out the rest. 2) Commit with a descriptive message that follows the repository's style (look at git log). 3) Push to the current branch; never force push and never switch branch. 4) If the project has a release or a GitHub Action to trigger (e.g. gh workflow run, npm publish) and the goal requires it, run it and report the outcome and links. In the summary, give the commit hash, branch, and the outcome of the push and actions. Outcome "ko" if a step fails.

app-web.label: Open in browser
app-web.hint: Starts the site (or uses one already running, e.g. on IIS) and opens it in the browser. Nothing to configure.

app-desktop.label: Launch desktop app
app-desktop.hint: Builds and launches the desktop app and keeps it open until you approve. Nothing to configure.

app-mobile.label: Show on phone
app-mobile.hint: Builds and installs the app (APK or iOS) on the connected phone and opens it. Nothing to configure.

collaudo-mobile.label: Acceptance test on phone
collaudo-mobile.hint: Builds and installs the app on the connected phone, tries it on the change's scenarios while following the app log, and reports anomalies.
collaudo-mobile.role: Acceptance tester: uses the app like a user and checks that the change works, without modifying the code.
collaudo-mobile.instructions: Test on the phone what was implemented, changed or fixed: pick the scenarios from the goal, the previous phases and git diff, run them on the app and report every anomaly. Do not perform irreversible actions (purchases, real sends, deleting data).

pr-commenti.label: PR points
pr-commenti.hint: Reads the comments of a pull request (GitHub, Azure DevOps) and lists them by priority: at approval you choose which ones to implement.
pr-commenti.role: Pull request reader: collects the review comments to apply, without changing the code.
pr-commenti.instructions: Read the given pull request and turn the review comments that are still open into points to implement, one per comment, with the original severity.

criteri-accettazione.label: Acceptance criteria
criteri-accettazione.hint: Reads the linked user story, proposes the acceptance criteria, compares them with those already there and points out missing specifications, in an HTML page ready to copy.
criteri-accettazione.role: Functional analyst: derives clear, testable acceptance criteria from the user story, without changing the code.
criteri-accettazione.instructions: Derive the acceptance criteria of the linked user story, compare them with those already there and point out the specifications missing to settle them. Look at the code only to understand the current behaviour and the constraints the user story takes for granted. If the goal asks for the Gherkin format, write the criteria as Given/When/Then.
